newsitem.title: EGYPT: Privatisation hiatus sends Egypt shares dipping.
newsitem.headline: Privatisation hiatus sends Egypt shares dipping.

text.p: Egyptian share prices ended slightly weaker on Monday as investors pulled out of a largely static market to buy into upcoming government privatisations, brokers said.
The Capital Market Authority all-share index slipped 0.2 percent to 387.19 points in mostly institutional trade which revolved around the favourite cement and milling sectors.

Private deals worth $14 million in rarely-traded firms Egyptians Abroad for Investment and Development and dollar-denominated Egyptian Maritime Transport/Martrans sent volume rocketing to 100 million pounds ($29.5 million).
"There's no reason for the market to go anywhere. Prices are not really falling but they're not rising either," said broker Youssef Khalil of Delta/EAB.
"Foreign investors are scarce and many local ones are selling what they see as static shares to buy into new issues."

Government newspapers have published lists of firms in which the state may soon sell a stake and on Tuesday, the state will offer the public at least 10 percent of partly-private realty firm Development and Engineering Consultancy DIPH.CA.

The privatisation drew investors attention to the housing sector, and both heavyweight firms Medinet Nasr Housing and Development and Heliopolis Housing and Development. Medinet Nasr shed 0.5 pounds to 490 while Heliopolis gained 6.01 to 445.
Development and Engineering Consultancy saw 1.6 million pounds of trading before falling 1.9 pounds to 36.19.

Investors continued to dabble in cements, but prices only firmed slightly. Amriyah Cement, the day's most active share with 5.1 million pounds of trade, rose 0.3 to 89.25 while Helwan Portland Cement HELW.CA gained 0.5 to 79.5.
Upper Egypt Flour Mills was one of the most traded in its sector, but stocks only rose 0.5 to 89 pounds.
Institutional buying in Nile Pharmaceutical and Chemicals brought activity to the quiet sector and stocks ended 0.5 up to 52.5 pounds.
The index for openly traded firms fell to 590.16 points from 593.13 points and the index for rarely traded "closed" firms fell to 270.19 from 270.25.
Of the 92 shares traded, 39 rose and 26 declined. The remaining 27 ended unchanged.
